Description: State the full name of the AI system

Description: Summarize the system's architecture, core components (e.g., model, APIs, databases), and technical functionality. Include whether the system is based on general-purpose AI models or tailored algorithms. Note if it operates autonomously or under human supervision.
Example write-up: SmartAid integrates a large language model (for symptom parsing), a logistic regression model (for triage scoring), and secure APIs for EHR integration. It operates in real-time, under direct supervision by clinical staff. While it automates risk estimation, final decision-making is always performed by a licensed human practitioner.
Your Response: booksy is a single-page web application built with React and powered by a Node.js backend. It integrates Groq-hosted Llama-70B for real-time story generation, LumaLabs’ Photon model for illustrations, and ElevenLabs for narration. Supabase manages data storage and authentication. The system operates interactively under direct human supervision, with families guiding story progression collaboratively.

Description: List the specific contexts, user needs, or operational environments for which the system was designed. Include the kinds of decisions, predictions, or outputs the system generates, and what user action (if any) it supports.
Example write-up: SmartAid is designed for use in hospital emergency departments to support triage nurses by generating risk scores and suggesting differential diagnoses. It analyzes patient-reported symptoms alongside historical EHR data and assists with prioritization and resource allocation decisions, without replacing clinical judgment.
Your Response: booksy is designed for families seeking meaningful, creative bonding experiences. It enables parents and children to co-create interactive storybooks by generating narratives, illustrations, and voiceovers in real time. The system supports collaborative decision-making through choose-your-own-adventure storytelling and preserves outputs as digital keepsakes for future reliving and sharing.

Description: Identify the primary audience or actors meant to operate, interact with, or rely on the system (e.g., clinicians, consumers, analysts). Clarify the level of expertise or training expected for responsible use.
Example write-up: SmartAid is intended for use by licensed emergency physicians and triage nurses with certified training on the system. Users must understand AI-assisted clinical decision tools and comply with institutional oversight protocols.
Your Response: booksy is intended for parents, children, and families who wish to create and share interactive stories together. No technical expertise or training is required—its child-friendly, intuitive design ensures responsible use by all ages.

Description: Describe any uses, domains, or environments where the system is not intended to be applied. Include foreseeable misuse scenarios that may raise safety, fairness concerns. These may include domains where the system is technically unreliable, lacks sufficient safeguards, or would create unacceptable risks.
Example write-up: SmartAid is not approved for use with pediatric patients, psychiatric evaluations, or for autonomous operation without clinician review. It is not intended for deployment in settings lacking integrated electronic health records or in jurisdictions where health data governance requirements are unmet.
Your Response: booksy is not intended for educational assessment, therapeutic use, or replacing parental interaction. It should not be used to generate inappropriate, harmful, or offensive content. The system is unsuitable in environments without responsible adult supervision or where child privacy and data security cannot be ensured.

Description: Describe each dataset used for your AI system if any. Include the purpose of the dataset, its size, source domains (e.g., medical records, social media), and whether the data represent diverse populations relevant to the intended use. Mention if the dataset includes personal or sensitive data and whether it was anonymized or synthesized.
Example write-up: Training data include 1.2 million anonymized emergency room cases from Canadian hospitals collected between 2016–2021. Validation used synthetic profiles generated via differential privacy. The dataset includes diverse demographic coverage by age, sex, and ethnicity but excludes biometric data. Sensitive fields (e.g., race, religion) were excluded from model input.
Your Response: booksy does not rely on proprietary datasets for training. AI-generated stories and illustrations are produced in real-time using general-purpose models (Llama-70B for text, Photon for images). Users provide personal inputs, such as names, voice recordings, and story choices, which are stored securely; all sensitive data is handled with consent and privacy safeguards.

Description: Explain how each dataset was collected, including the data sources (e.g., surveys, web scraping), consent mechanisms, and whether third parties were involved. Clarify any limitations or assumptions made during collection and whether the data were collected directly from individuals or derived from secondary sources.
Example write-up: Training data were collected under research ethics approvals with informed consent where required. EHRs were extracted through secure hospital channels. Supplemental data were synthesized using a GPT-based generator and underwent internal validation. All data were anonymized using irreversible hashing techniques before model access.
Your Response: booksy does not collect external datasets. All user-provided inputs, such as story text, names, and audio recordings, are entered directly by families with consent. No third-party data is used, and all personal content is stored securely for the purpose of creating and replaying stories.

Description: Detail the methods used to detect and reduce bias in data and model behavior. Include audits, rebalancing techniques, adversarial testing, subgroup performance analysis, and any manual interventions. Explain how outcomes were validated for fairness across different demographic groups.
Example write-up: Bias audits were conducted pre-deployment using subgroup fairness metrics. Underrepresented populations were oversampled. The model was adjusted using threshold optimization to equalize false negative rates. Performance disparities >2% triggered model retraining. Post-deployment dashboards monitor demographic drift monthly.
Your Response: booksy incorporates bias mitigation by filtering AI-generated content to avoid stereotypes or harmful narratives. Prompts and outputs are reviewed to ensure inclusivity across cultures, genders, and ages. User testing with diverse families helps validate fairness, and moderation tools flag inappropriate or biased content in real time.

Example write-up: Use is geographically limited to Canada and the EU. SmartAid cannot be deployed in jurisdictions with conflicting privacy laws. Only certified hospital IT environments with VPN access are permitted. Unauthorized modification or repurposing of model outputs is prohibited by system policy and licensing.

Unauthorized redistribution, reverse engineering, or use for harmful content creation is prohibited and mitigated through access controls and moderation features.

Story generation latency averages under 2 seconds, with illustrations and narration synchronized in real time. User satisfaction surveys indicate high engagement and perceived enjoyment, while moderation tools maintain content appropriateness and fairness across diverse users.

Section: Evaluations for Edge Cases or Adversarial Inputs
Description: Detail evaluations conducted to assess the system's behavior under rare, extreme, or adversarial conditions. Include examples of inputs used, failure cases identified, and robustness strategies employed. Clarify any known limitations in edge performance and how these are mitigated.
Example write-up: The system was tested using synthetic adversarial cases (e.g., conflicting symptoms, ambiguous phrasing). A known failure mode involves conflating panic attacks with myocardial infarction. A hybrid rule-based post-filtering layer was added to flag high-ambiguity predictions for manual review.
Your Response: booksy was evaluated with unusual or challenging inputs, such as nonsensical story prompts, extremely long text entries, or atypical character names. Known limitations include occasional narrative inconsistencies or mismatched illustrations, which are mitigated through prompt refinement, moderation filters, and real-time user guidance.

Description: Identify risks the system may pose to health, safety, privacy, fundamental rights, or equity—especially in the context of foreseeable misuse. Include both technical and societal risks, noting affected groups (e.g., children, economically vulnerable populations). Highlight severity and likelihood.
Example write-up: Risks include potential misclassification in ambiguous presentations, delays in care if risk is underestimated, and exposure of personal health data in poorly configured installations. Vulnerable populations may be disproportionately impacted without ongoing fairness checks and clinician oversight.
Your Response: Potential risks of booksy include exposure of personal data if accounts are shared or mismanaged, creation of inappropriate or biased content, and reduced parental engagement if over-reliance on AI occurs. Children are the primary affected group, though severity is moderate and likelihood mitigated through supervision and content moderation.

Description: Summarize specific measures taken to prevent or mitigate the risks identified above. Include technical safeguards (e.g., red-teaming, input validation), process changes (e.g., oversight committees), or external interventions (e.g., third-party audits). Indicate the timeline and responsible parties for implementation.
Example write-up: To mitigate risks, SmartAid includes clinician override, confidence thresholds, and real-time logging. All decisions can be traced for audit. Regular third-party audits, monthly internal reviews, and fairness alerting dashboards are in place. All safety-critical updates require pre-approval from the compliance board.
Your Response: To mitigate risks, booksy implements content moderation filters, input validation, and real-time supervision by parents or guardians. AI outputs are reviewed through user testing and diverse prompts. The development team monitors and updates safeguards continuously, with all updates deployed after internal review and testing.

Description: Describe ways in which the system could be used improperly or outside its intended context, including foreseeable misuse that may result in safety risks, rights violations, or discriminatory outcomes. These risks are mitigated via license enforcement, update verification, and runtime checks that restrict operation outside approved configurations.
